description: DONE (folded 2026-07-03 as <fill>, two-lane audited + focused re-audit PASS after one FAIL-and-rework). Region::MapKeyPresent in branch_possible (jobs/semantic.rs) was hardcoded true for BOTH the key-present and key-absent edges (unlike sibling regions Type/Equal/TupleArity/List which prune via intersect/is_subtype). The dead trailing catch-all clause (pick(_) -> :unreachable) therefore leaked :unreachable into the first tuple position. FIX: prune the miss edge ONLY when the key is a resolvable atom singleton AND the source PROVABLY carries it (source <: map({key:any}), reusing the sibling-region intersect/is_subtype shape); MapSig is an open-record lower bound so this is the correct proof. Prune SHAPE audit-verified sound (no over-prune on open/union maps — the miss edge stays live when the key isn't provably present). Filled map_pattern_binding_flows_into_selected_leaf with {int, :none}, mutation-verified. REGRESSION CAUGHT+FIXED in rework: the first cut used .expect() on as_map_key, which panics the COMPILER on int/float/string/nil map-pattern keys (as_int_singleton is a permanent stub; int_lit collapses literals) — valid programs that compiled before, invisible to CI (no fixture matched a map on a non-atom key). Fixed with an unprovable-implies-true fallback (if let Some(map_key) = as_map_key {prune} else {true}), restoring the pre-existing safe behavior for non-atom keys. Added regression fixture 00553_match_map_nonatom_keys.fz (int+float+string keys) + test, mutation-proven (naked .expect panics, fallback compiles); re-audit confirmed all 5 key types (int/float/string/nil/bool) now compile. Numbered 00553 (end of sort order) to avoid reshuffling the index%4 corpus shards. 1166/0/24. NOTE: fz-go4.36 (guard-clause non-narrowing, the sibling bug) is DIAGNOSED-ONLY and stays OPEN — architectural (numeric-literal erasure at ActivationKey), not a point fix.
title: Dead catch-all clause leaks :unreachable into first tuple position (map-pattern proof narrowing)
